  • ReviewGuard: Aligning LLM-Assisted Peer Review with Long-Term Scientific Impact

    ReviewGuard：将法学硕士协助的同行评审与长期科学影响相结合

    Abdur Rasool, Xiaohui Huang, Yanqing Hu, Linyi Yang
    cs.AI cs.DL

    同行评审是科学质量控制的核心，但它可能会低估后来取得重大引用影响的论文。虽然前沿大型语言模型在同行评审自动化方面表现出了希望，但它们主要模仿人类评审者的偏好，而不是预测长期的科学价值。我们引入了 ReviewGuard，这是一个两阶段的框架，它将法学硕士生成的评论与基于引用的长期科学影响估计（而不是同时的审稿人判断）结合起来。在 OpenReview 的 20,861 篇 AI/ML 论文中，添加了语义学者引文数据，ReviewGuard 与被拒绝然后发表的论文的未来引用实现了 \r{ho} = 0.776 的 Spearman 相关性，优于人类审稿人 (\r{ho} = 0.492) 和监督专家模型 (\r{ho} = 0.681)。在相同的决策阈值下，ReviewGuard 标记了 10.2% 的高影响力被拒绝论文，而人类审稿人的标记为 1.8%，相当于提高了 5.6 倍。我们的结果表明，影响力一致的强化学习可以为编辑提供补充信号，以识别高潜力的作品，而无需取代人类的判断。

    Show English abstract

    Peer review is central to scientific quality control, yet it can undervalue papers that later achieve substantial citation impact. While frontier large language models have shown promise in automating aspects of peer review, they primarily mimic human reviewer preferences rather than predict long-term scientific value. We introduce ReviewGuard, a two-stage framework that aligns LLM-generated reviews with citation-based estimates of long-term scientific impact rather than contemporaneous reviewer judgments. On 20,861 AI/ML papers from OpenReview augmented with Semantic Scholar citation data, ReviewGuard achieves a Spearman correlation of \r{ho} = 0.776 with future citations on rejected-then-published papers, outperforming human reviewers (\r{ho} = 0.492) and a supervised Expert model (\r{ho} = 0.681). Under the same decision threshold, ReviewGuard flags 10.2% of high-impact rejected papers, compared with 1.8% for human reviewers, corresponding to a 5.6x improvement. Our results demonstrate that impact-aligned reinforcement learning can provide editors with a complementary signal for identifying high-potential work, without replacing human judgment.

  • Type Checking Project Haystack Grids using JSON Schema and Pydantic

    使用 JSON Schema 和 Pydantic 对项目 Haystack 网格进行类型检查

    Thomas Hirsch, Samina Kadkhoda Masoumali, Gerald Schweiger
    cs.AI cs.PL cs.SE

    本体通过支持互操作性和自动化来实现建筑物中可扩展的能源服务。 Haystack 项目是一种构建本体，由于其灵活的、基于标签的语义模型、开放性和可扩展性而被广泛采用，但存在标签使用不明确和自动化验证有限的问题。尽管 Project Haystack 已正式开放，但它对源自 Haxall 生态系统的自定义文件格式和特定​​领域语言的依赖对集成造成了事实上的障碍。在本文中，我们通过引入基于 Python 的 Haystack 工具链来解决这些限制。我们提出了 (i) Haystack 定义文件（Trio 文件格式）的解析器，以及 (ii) 一个代码生成器，可以从这些解析的规范中派生 Pydantic 模型和 JSON 模式定义。生成的模型支持静态类型检查，并支持 Python 内 Haystack 网格的结构验证，以及 Python 生态系统外部 JSON 表示的基于模式的验证。所有工具、生成的模型和模式都是在开源许可下公开发布的，目的是加强 Haystack 生态系统并开辟一条超越其当前技术边界的实用途径。

    Show English abstract

    Ontologies enable scalable energy services in buildings by supporting interoperability and automation. Project Haystack is a building ontology that is widely adopted due to its flexible, tag-based semantic model, openness, and extensibility, but suffers from ambiguous tag usage and limited automated validation. Although Project Haystack is formally open, its reliance on custom file formats and domain-specific languages that originate from the Haxall ecosystem creates a de facto barrier to integration. In this paper, we address these limitations by introducing a Python-based toolchain for Haystack. We present (i) a parser for Haystack definition files (Trio file format), and (ii) a code generator that derives Pydantic models and JSON Schema definitions from these parsed specifications. The resulting models enable static type checking and enable structural validation of Haystack grids within Python, as well as schema-based validation of JSON representations outside the Python ecosystem. All tools, generated models, and schemas are released publicly under an open-source license, with the goal of strengthening the Haystack ecosystem and opening a practical pathway beyond its current technical boundaries.

  • Small edits, large models: How Wikipedia advocacy shapes LLM values

    小编辑，大模型：维基百科的倡导如何塑造法学硕士价值观

    Jasmine Brazilek, Maria Navas, Alexa Gnauck
    cs.AI cs.CL cs.CY

    一小群志愿者能否仅通过编辑维基百科来塑造人工智能系统讨论动物福利的方式？我们证明他们可以。维基百科出现在几乎所有主要语言模型训练数据集中，并且比网络爬虫文本的权重更大。亲动物维基百科 (PAW) 是一群倡导者，他们将源自动物福利的内容添加到相关文章中，在 115 个页面上进行了 125 次编辑。使用基于梯度的数据归因（Bergson；MAGIC），我们追踪了这些编辑如何影响语言模型行为。 Llama 3.1 8B 上的 TrackStar 检索归因发现，PAW 编辑的部分占动物福利查询最高属性文档的 68% (p < 0.0001)，但对于同一公司的不相关查询仅占 52% (p = 0.53)：该模型将 PAW 内容专门链接到动物福利主题，而不是一般实体。对 Llama-3.2-1B 的 MAGIC 反事实影响力估计，在五个随机训练顺序种子中运行，更清晰地给出了相同的情况：在每个种子中，对动物福利查询最有影响力的前 10 个文档都是 PAW 编辑（10 个种子中的 10 个，5 个种子中的 5 个），而在一般查询中，相同的前 10 个文档是偶然的（10 个种子中的 4 到 6 个）。 PAW 的平均影响力超过了对动物福利查询的平均控制影响力，每个种子的 p < 0.0001，其影响比一般查询大 6 至 30 倍。对于所有 10 次运行，保留子集验证得出 Spearman rho = 1.00。当我们对 PAW 内容与对照内容的单独模型进行微调时，每个模型在其训练的文本类型上表现得更好：PAW 训练的模型将动物福利文本的困惑度从 12.4 降低到 8.4，而对照训练的模型将对照文本的困惑度从 16.1 降低到 11.4。因此，小型、协调的维基百科编辑活动可以衡量语言模型如何处理这些编辑所涉及的主题。

    Show English abstract

    Can a small group of volunteers shape how AI systems discuss animal welfare, just by editing Wikipedia? We show that they can. Wikipedia appears in nearly every major language model training dataset and is weighted more heavily than web-crawled text. The Pro-Animal Wikipedians (PAW), a group of advocates who add sourced animal welfare content to relevant articles, have made 125 edits across 115 pages. Using gradient-based data attribution (Bergson; MAGIC), we traced how these edits influence language model behavior. TrackStar retrieval attribution on Llama 3.1 8B found that PAW-edited sections made up 68 percent of the highest-attributed documents for animal welfare queries (p < 0.0001) but only 52 percent for unrelated queries about the same companies (p = 0.53): the model links PAW content specifically to animal welfare topics, not to the entities in general. MAGIC counterfactual influence estimation on Llama-3.2-1B, run across five random training-order seeds, gave the same picture even more sharply: in every seed, the top-10 most influential documents on animal welfare queries were all PAW edits (10 of 10, 5 of 5 seeds), while on general queries the same top-10 sat at chance (4 to 6 of 10). Mean PAW influence exceeded mean control influence on animal welfare queries with p < 0.0001 in every seed, an effect 6 to 30 times larger than on general queries. Leave-subset-out validation gave Spearman rho = 1.00 for all 10 runs. When we fine-tuned separate models on PAW content versus control content, each model performed better specifically on the type of text it was trained on: the PAW-trained model cut perplexity on animal welfare text from 12.4 to 8.4, while the control-trained model cut perplexity on control text from 16.1 to 11.4. A small, coordinated Wikipedia editing campaign therefore measurably shapes how language models handle the topics those edits address.
